<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sony&#8217;s management uses this measure to review operating trends, perform analytical comparisons and assess whether its structural transformation initiatives are achieving their objectives. <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>This supplemental non-U.S. GAAP measure should be considered in addition to, not as a substitute for, Sony&#8217;s operating income in accordance with U.S. GAAP.</font></div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">*&#160;&#160;U.S. dollar amounts have been translated from yen, for convenience only, at the rate of 83 yen=1 U.S. dollar, the approximate Tokyo foreign exchange market rate as of March 31, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">**&#160;&#160;Sony is undertaking structural transformation initiatives to enhance profitability through implementation of various cost reduction programs as well as adoption of horizontal platforms.&#160;&#160;Restructuring charges are recorded, depending on the nature of the individual items, in cost of sales, selling, general and administrative expenses as well as (gain) loss on sale, disposal or impairment of assets and other, net, in the consolidated statement of income.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">*** The 27.1 billion yen loss on impairment, a non-cash charge recorded within operating income in the previous fiscal year, primarily reflected a decrease in the estimated fair value of property, plant and equipment, and certain intangible assets.&#160;&#160;Sony has excluded the loss on impairment from restructuring charges as it is not directly related to Sony&#8217;s restructuring initiatives.&#160;&#160;Sony defines restructuring initiatives as activities initiated by Sony, such as exiting a business or product category or implementing a headcount reduction program, which are designed to generate a positive impact on future profitability.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sony realigned its reportable segments from the first quarter of the fiscal year ended March 31, 2011 to reflect modifications to the organizational structure as of April 1, 2010, primarily repositioning the operations of the previously reported B2B &amp; Disc Manufacturing segment.&#160;&#160;In connection with this realignment, the Consumer Products &amp; Devices segment was renamed the Consumer, Professional &amp; Devices (&#8220;CPD&#8221;) segment.&#160;&#160;The CPD segment includes televisions, digital imaging, audio and video, semiconductors and components as well as professional solutions (the B2B business which was previously included in the B2B &amp; Disc Manufacturing segment).&#160;&#160;The equity results of S-LCD Corporation (&#8220;S-LCD&#8221;), a joint venture with Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd., are also included within the CPD segment.&#160;&#160;The disc manufacturing business previously included in the B2B &amp; Disc Manufacturing segment is now included in All Other.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Networked Products &amp; Services (&#8220;NPS&#8221;), Pictures, Music and Financial Services segments remain unchanged.&#160;&#160;The equity earnings from Sony Ericsson Mobile Communications AB (&#8220;Sony Ericsson&#8221;) continue to be presented as a separate segment.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In connection with this realignment, both the sales and operating revenue (&#8220;sales&#8221;) and operating income (loss) of each segment in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2010 have been revised to conform to the current presentation.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Consolidated Results for the Fiscal Year Ended March 31, 2011</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Sales</font> were 7,181.3 billion yen (86,521 million U.S. dollars), a decrease of 0.5% compared to the previous fiscal year (&#8220;year-on-year&#8221;), primarily due to a decrease in sales in all segments except the CPD and NPS segments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the fiscal year ended March 31, 2011, the average rate of the yen was 84.7 yen against the U.S. dollar and 111.6 yen against the euro, which was 8.4% and 16.2% higher, respectively, than the previous year.&#160;&#160;On a local currency basis, sales increased 6% year-on-year.&#160;&#160;For references to sales on a local currency basis, see Note on page 10.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Operating income</font> increased 168.0 billion yen year-on-year to 199.8 billion yen (2,407 million U.S. dollars) despite a large unfavorable impact of foreign exchange rates.&#160;&#160;The significant increase in operating income was mainly due to an improvement in operating results in the NPS and CPD segments.&#160;&#160;Excluding equity in net income (loss) of affiliated companies, restructuring charges and a non-cash charge related to LCD television asset impairment, operating income on an as adjusted basis increased 39.4 billion yen to 252.8 billion yen (3,046 million U.S. dollars) year-on-year.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Equity in net income of affiliated companies</font>, recorded within operating income, was 14.1 billion yen (169 million U.S. dollars)<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>compared to equity in net loss of 30.2 billion yen in the previous fiscal year.&#160;&#160;Sony recorded equity in net income for Sony Ericsson of 4.2 billion yen (50 million U.S. dollars) compared to equity in net loss of 34.5 billion yen in the previous fiscal year.&#160;&#160;Equity in net income for S-LCD increased 6.8 billion yen to 7.2 billion yen (87 million U.S. dollars).</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the fiscal year ended March 31, 2011, Sony recorded charges of 11.9 billion yen (143 million U.S. dollars), consisting principally of idle facility costs at manufacturing sites and an incremental provision for life insurance policy reserves, caused by the Great East Japan Earthquake (the &#8220;Earthquake&#8221;) that occurred on March 11, 2011.&#160;&#160;In addition, there was a 5.1 billion yen (61 million U.S. dollars) impact from the estimated net margin loss associated with a decrease in sales resulting from the Earthquake and an estimate of variable costs.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, Sony incurred incremental expenses, including restoration costs (e.g., repair, removal and cleaning costs) directly related to the damages caused by the disaster to certain fixed assets including buildings, machinery and equipment as well as inventories at manufacturing sites and warehouses, in addition to charges for the disposal or impairment of fixed assets and inventories.&#160;&#160;The impact of these expenses was 10.9 billion yen (131 million U.S. dollars); however, Sony has insurance policies that cover certain damages to fixed assets and inventories as well as the associated restoration costs, which are expected to offset almost all of these losses and expenses in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2011, as the recoveries from insurance claims are deemed probable.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The net effect of<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"> other income and expenses</font> was income of 5.2 billion yen (63 million U.S. dollars), an improvement of 10.1 billion yen year-on-year, primarily due to the recording of a net foreign exchange gain in the current fiscal year compared to the recording of a net foreign exchange loss in the previous fiscal year.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Income before income taxes</font> increased 178.1 billion yen to 205.0 billion yen (2,470 million U.S. dollars).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Income taxes</font>: For the current fiscal year, Sony recorded 425.3 billion yen (5,125 million U.S. dollars) of income taxes, primarily resulting from the recording of a non-cash charge to establish a valuation allowance of 362.3 billion yen (4,365 million U.S. dollars) against certain deferred tax assets in Japan.&#160;&#160;Sony evaluates its deferred tax assets on a tax jurisdiction basis to determine if a valuation allowance is required.&#160;&#160;In Japan, Sony Corporation files a stand-alone tax filing for local tax purposes and a consolidated national tax filing with its wholly-owned Japanese subsidiaries for national tax purposes.&#160;&#160;Sony Corporation and its national tax filing group in Japan are in a three year cumulative loss as of March 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;Under U.S. GAAP, a three year cumulative loss is considered significant negative evidence regarding the realizability of deferred tax assets, which is difficult to overcome, particularly given the relatively short tax loss carry forward period of seven years in Japan and the adverse impact of the Earthquake on the near-term forecast for entities in Japan.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, Sony determined in the fourth quarter of the fiscal year ended March 31, 2011 that it was required under U.S. GAAP to establish a valuation allowance against certain deferred tax assets in Japan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The non-cash charge to establish a valuation allowance does not have any impact on Sony&#8217;s consolidated operating income or cash flow, nor does such an allowance preclude Sony from using the loss carry forwards or other deferred tax assets in the future.&#160;&#160;It is also important to note that the establishment of this valuation allowance does not reflect a change in Sony&#8217;s view of its long-term corporate strategy.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Unless otherwise specified, all amounts are on a U.S. GAAP basis.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Sales</font> increased 1.6 % year-on-year (a 10% increase on a local currency basis) to 3,572.7 billion yen (43,045 million U.S. dollars).&#160;&#160;(Sales to outside customers increased 4.3% year-on-year.)&#160;&#160;This was primarily due to higher LCD television sales resulting from a significant increase in unit sales that came mostly from the Asia-Pacific, Other Areas, and Japan and higher semiconductor sales resulting from strong performance of small- and medium-sized LCD panels and image sensors.&#160;&#160;The sales increase was partially offset by lower components sales resulting from a decrease in sales of storage media affected by market contraction and a decrease in sales of optical disc drives driven by price competition.&#160;&#160;LCD television sales in Japan increased primarily due to both a program which provided consumers with a subsidy from the Japanese government and enhanced demand resulting from the transition from analog to digital television broadcasting in Japan which was scheduled to be completed by July 2011.&#160;&#160;The subsidy program ended on March 31, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Operating income</font> of 2.9 billion yen (35 million U.S. dollars) was recorded, compared to a loss of 53.2 billion yen in the previous fiscal year.&#160;&#160;This improvement was driven primarily by an increase in gross profit due to higher sales, a decrease in loss on sale, disposal or impairment of assets and other (net), and a decrease in restructuring charges.&#160;&#160;These factors were partially offset by unfavorable foreign exchange rates and an increase in selling, general and administrative expenses primarily associated with higher marketing expenses.&#160;&#160;In the previous fiscal year, a 27.1 billion yen non-cash charge related to LCD television asset impairment, not included in restructuring charges, was recorded.&#160;&#160;(For reference to LCD television asset impairment, see note *** on page 2.)&#160;&#160;Restructuring charges were 41.6 billion yen (501 million U.S. dollars) in the current fiscal year, compared with 75.9 billion yen recorded in the previous fiscal year.&#160;&#160;The current fiscal year&#8217;s restructuring charges included expenses of 11.6 billion yen (140 million U.S. dollars) related to the transfer to third parties of the Barcelona factory in Europe and its asset impairment (executed in January 2011).&#160;&#160;Categories that favorably impacted the change in segment operating results (excluding restructuring charges) include semiconductors, reflecting an increase in sales of image sensors, and professional solutions, reflecting an increase in sales of products such as digital cinema projectors.&#160;&#160;A category that unfavorably impacted the change in segment operating results (excluding restructuring charges) was LCD televisions, reflecting a decline in unit selling prices and unfavorable foreign exchange rates, despite rising unit sales.</font></div>

<td nowrap valign="bottom" width="1%" style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></td>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Unless otherwise specified, all amounts are on a U.S. GAAP basis.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Sales </font>increased 0.4% year-on-year (a 9% increase on a local currency basis) to 1,579.3 billion yen (19,028 million U.S. dollars).&#160;&#160;(Sales to outside customers decreased 1.2% year-on-year.)&#160;&#160;&#160;Unfavorable foreign exchange rates offset increased sales mainly in PCs, which saw increased unit sales and an expanding market share in all regions, resulting in segment sales that were almost flat year-on year.</font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: -1.7pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Unless otherwise specified, all amounts are reported on a U.S. GAAP basis. The results presented above are a yen-translation of the results of Sony Pictures Entertainment (&#8220;SPE&#8221;), a U.S.-based operation that aggregates the results of its worldwide subsidiaries on a U.S. dollar basis.&#160;&#160;Management analyzes the results of SPE in U.S. dollars, so discussion of certain portions of its results is specified as being on &#8220;a U.S. dollar basis.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Sales</font> decreased 14.9% year-on-year (an 8% decrease on a U.S. dollar basis) to 600.0 billion yen (7,229 million U.S. dollars), primarily due to lower motion picture revenues and the appreciation of the yen against the U.S. dollar.&#160;&#160;While the current year benefitted from the strong performances of <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">The Karate Kid</font>,<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline"> Grown Ups </font>and <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Salt</font>, international theatrical and worldwide home entertainment revenues declined significantly in comparison to the previous fiscal year, which included <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">2012</font>, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Angels &amp; Demons</font> and <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Michael Jackson&#8217;s This Is It</font>.&#160;&#160;On a U.S. dollar basis, television revenues increased due to higher subscription and advertising revenues from a number of international channels and higher U.S. revenues from cable and syndication programming.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Operating income</font> decreased 4.1 billion yen year-on-year to 38.7 billion yen (466 million U.S. dollars), primarily due to the appreciation of the yen against the U.S. dollar.&#160;&#160;On a U.S. dollar basis, operating income was almost flat year-on-year as lower home entertainment revenues from motion picture catalog product and the theatrical underperformance of <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">How Do You Know</font> were offset by<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>the higher television revenues mentioned above.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In March 2011, SPE acquired an additional 5% equity interest and a controlling interest, including certain management rights, in the Game Show Network, LLC (&#8220;GSN&#8221;), which operates a U.S. cable network and online business. As a result, SPE&#8217;s total equity interest in GSN increased to 40%.&#160;&#160;In accordance with the accounting guidance for business combinations achieved in stages, Sony remeasured the 35% equity interest in GSN that it owned prior to the acquisition at the fair value of such interest at the time control was obtained.&#160;&#160;This resulted in the recognition of a gain of 27.0 billion yen (325 million U.S. dollars), which is included in the current fiscal year&#8217;s operating income.&#160;&#160;The current fiscal year&#8217;s operating income also includes a gain on the sale of SPE&#8217;s remaining equity interest in a Latin American premium pay television business (HBO Latin America).&#160;&#160;The total gain recognized from these two transactions was 30.3 billion yen (365 million U.S. dollars).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: -1.7pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Unless otherwise specified, all amounts are reported on a U.S. GAAP basis. The results presented above include the yen-translated results of SME, a U.S. based operation which aggregates the results of its worldwide subsidiaries on a U.S. dollar basis, the results of SMEJ, a Japan based music company which aggregates its results in yen, and the yen-translated consolidated results of Sony/ATV, a 50% owned U.S. based joint venture in the music publishing business which aggregates the results of its worldwide subsidiaries on a U.S. dollar basis.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Sales</font> decreased 9.9% year-on-year (a 5% decrease on a local currency basis) to 470.7 billion yen (5,672 million U.S. dollars).&#160;&#160;This decrease was primarily due to the negative impact of the appreciation of the yen against the U.S. dollar, the especially strong performance of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Michael Jackson product</font> in the previous fiscal year and the continued contraction of the physical music market.&#160;&#160;Best selling titles during the current year included ikimono-gakari&#8217;s <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">IKIMONO BAKARI: MEMBERS&#8217; BEST SELECTION</font>, Susan Boyle&#8217;s <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">The Gift</font>, P!nk&#8217;s <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Greatest Hits &#8230; So Far!!!</font>, Michael Jackson&#8217;s <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Michael</font> and music from the cast of the hit television show <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Glee</font>.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Operating income</font> increased 2.4 billion yen year-on-year to 38.9 billion yen (469 million U.S. dollars).&#160;&#160;Despite the decrease in sales, operating income increased due to decreases in marketing, restructuring and overhead costs.</font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In Sony&#8217;s Financial Services segment, the results include Sony Financial Holdings, Inc. (&#8220;SFH&#8221;) and SFH&#8217;s consolidated subsidiaries such as Sony Life Insurance Co., Ltd. (&#8220;Sony Life&#8221;), Sony Assurance Inc. and Sony Bank Inc. (&#8220;Sony Bank&#8221;), as well as the results for Sony Finance International Inc. (&#8220;SFI&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Unless otherwise specified, all amounts are reported on a U.S. GAAP basis.&#160;&#160;Therefore, the results of Sony Life discussed below differ from the results that SFH and Sony Life disclose separately on a Japanese statutory basis.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Financial services revenue</font> decreased 5.3% year-on-year to 806.5 billion yen (9,717 million U.S. dollars), primarily due to a decrease in revenue at Sony Life.&#160;&#160;Revenue at Sony Life decreased 5.9% year-on-year to 696.7 billion yen (8,393 million U.S. dollars), primarily due to investment performance.&#160;&#160;The decrease in revenue at Sony Life was partially offset by an increase in revenue from insurance premiums, reflecting a steady increase in policy amount in force.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Operating income </font>decreased 43.7 billion yen year-on-year to 118.8 billion yen (1,432 million U.S. dollars), primarily due to a decrease in operating income at Sony Life.&#160;&#160;Operating income at Sony Life decreased 48.9 billion yen year-on-year to 117.7 billion yen (1,418 million U.S. dollars).&#160;&#160;The decrease was mainly due to recording of net valuation gains from investments in convertible bonds in the general account in the previous fiscal year resulting from a significant rise in the Japanese stock market, and an increase in the provision of policy reserves for variable insurance in the separate account, driven primarily by a decline in the Japanese stock market in the current fiscal year.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sales<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>for the year ended March 31, 2011 decreased 6.5% year-on-year to 6,034 million euro.&#160;&#160;This decrease was due to a decline in unit shipments as a result of a focus on high-end smartphones and reduction in size of the product portfolio.&#160;&#160;Income before taxes of 133 million euro was recorded for the current year, compared to a loss before taxes of 654 million euro in the previous year.&#160;&#160;This improvement was mainly due to the positive impact of a rise in the average selling price, a favorable product mix and improved cost structure.&#160;&#160;In addition, there was a benefit relating to the reversal of warranty reserves.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows and charts showing Sony&#8217;s cash flow information for all segments, all segments excluding the Financial Services segment and the Financial Services segment alone, please refer to pages F-5 and F-14 respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Operating Activities:</font> During the current fiscal year, there was a net cash inflow of 616.2 billion yen (7,425 million U.S. dollars), a decrease of 296.7 billion yen, or 32.5% year-on-year.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For all segments excluding the Financial Services segment, there was a net cash inflow of 255.8 billion yen (3,082 million U.S. dollars) for the current fiscal year, a decrease of 314.4 billion yen, or 55.1% year-on-year.&#160;&#160;This net cash inflow was mainly due to a cash contribution from net income after taking into account depreciation, amortization and deferred income taxes as well as a decrease in notes and accounts receivable, trade.&#160;&#160;The inflow was partially offset by an increase in inventories.&#160;&#160;The year-on-year decrease in net cash inflow was mainly due to a decrease in notes and accounts payable, trade and an increase of inventories, partially offset by an improvement of net income (loss) after taking into account depreciation, amortization and deferred income taxes and a decrease in notes and accounts receivable, trade.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Financial Services segment had a net cash inflow of 369.5 billion yen (4,451 million U.S. dollars), an increase of 21.4 billion yen, or 6.2% year-on-year.&#160;&#160;This net cash inflow was generated primarily due to an increase in revenue from insurance premiums as a result of a steady increase in policy amount in force at Sony Life.&#160;&#160;Compared with the previous fiscal year, net cash inflow increased primarily due to an increase in cash contribution from net income after excluding the impact of gains or losses on revaluation of marketable securities held for trading purpose as well as on revaluation or impairment of securities investments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><br>
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Investing Activities:</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>During the current fiscal year, Sony used 714.4 billion yen (8,608 million U.S. dollars) of net cash in investing activities, a decrease of 31.6 billion yen, or 4.2% year-on-year.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Financial Services segment used 552.9 billion yen (6,661 million U.S. dollars) of net cash, an increase of 77.2 billion yen, or 16.2% year-on-year.&#160;&#160;During the current fiscal year, payments for investments and advances, carried out primarily at Sony Life and Sony Bank, where operations are expanding, exceeded proceeds from the maturities of marketable securities, sales of securities investments and collections of advances.&#160;&#160;The net cash outflow during the current fiscal year was partially offset by proceeds from the deconsolidation of a lease and rental business at SFI.&#160;&#160;The net cash used within the Financial Services segment increased year-on-year primarily due to a decrease in proceeds from the maturities of marketable securities, sales of securities investments and collections of advances.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In all segments excluding the Financial Services segment, net cash generated by operating and investing activities combined* for the current fiscal year was 118.3 billion yen (1,425 million U.S. dollars), a decrease of 204.0 billion yen, or 63.3% year-on-year.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Financing Activities: </font>During the current fiscal year, 10.1 billion yen (122 million U.S. dollars) of net cash was used in financing activities, compared to 365.0 billion yen generated in the previous fiscal year.&#160;&#160;For all segments excluding the Financial Services segment, there was 186.9 billion yen (2,251 million U.S. dollars) of net cash outflow, compared to a net cash inflow of 98.6 billion yen in the previous fiscal year.&#160;&#160;This was primarily due to significantly higher levels of both issuances of long-term corporate bonds and borrowings from banks in the previous fiscal year.&#160;&#160;There were no comparable issuances or borrowings during the current fiscal year; in addition, there was a 104.9 billion yen (1,264 million U.S. dollars) redemption of domestic straight bonds and a 52.0 billion yen (627 million U.S. dollars) repayment of a syndicated loan during the current fiscal year.&#160;&#160;In the Financial Services segment, financing activities generated 143.7 billion yen (1,731 million U.S. dollars) of net cash, a decrease of 94.9 billion yen, or 39.8% year-on-year, primarily due to a smaller increase in deposits from customers at Sony Bank and increased repayments of long-term debt.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Total Cash and Cash Equivalents:</font> Accounting for the above factors and the effect of fluctuations in exchange rates, the total outstanding balance of cash and cash equivalents at March 31, 2011 was 1,014.4 billion yen (12,222 million U.S. dollars).&#160;&#160;Cash and cash equivalents of all segments excluding the Financial Services segment was 847.4 billion yen (10,210 million U.S. dollars) at March 31, 2011, a decrease of 137.5 billion yen, or 14.0%, compared with the balance as of March 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;This was an increase of 73.5 billion yen, or 9.5%, compared with the balance as of December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Sony believes it continues to maintain sufficient liquidity through access to a total, translated into yen, of 755.2 billion yen (9,099 million U.S. dollars) of unused committed lines of credit with financial institutions in addition to the cash and cash equivalents balance at March 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;Within the Financial Services segment, the outstanding balance of cash and cash equivalents was 167.0 billion yen (2,012 million U.S. dollars) at March 31, 2011, a decrease of 39.7 billion yen, or 19.2%, compared with the balance as of March 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;This was an increase of 21.1 billion yen, or 14.5%, compared with the balance as of December 31, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">*&#160;&#160;Sony has included the information for cash flow from operating and investing activities combined excluding the Financial Services segment&#8217;s activities, as management frequently monitors this financial measure, and believes this non-U.S. GAAP measurement is important for use in evaluating Sony&#8217;s ability to generate cash to <font style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 9.5pt">maintain liquidity and fund debt principal and dividend payments from business activities other than its Financial Services segment.&#160;&#160;This information is derived from the reconciliations prepared in the Condensed Statements of Cash Flows on page F-14.&#160;&#160;This information and the separate condensed presentations shown below are not required or prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP.&#160;&#160;The Financial Services segment&#8217;s cash flow is excluded from the measure because SFH, which constitutes a majority of the Financial Services segment, is a separate publicly traded entity in Japan with a significant minority interest and it, as well as its subsidiaries, secure liquidity on their own.&#160;&#160;This measure may not be comparable to those of other companies.&#160;&#160;This measure has limitations, because it does not represent residual cash flows available for discretionary expenditures principally due to the fact that the measure does not deduct</font> the principal payments required for debt service.&#160;&#160;Therefore, Sony believes it is important to view this measure as supplemental to its entire statement of cash flows and together with Sony&#8217;s disclosures regarding investments, available credit facilities and overall liquidity.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Consolidated Results for the Fourth Quarter ended March 31, 2011</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Sales</font> for<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>the fourth quarter ended March 31, 2011 decreased 7.8% to 1,580.8 billion yen (19,046 million U.S. dollars) compared to the same quarter of the previous fiscal year.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the current quarter, the average rate of the yen was 81.3 yen against the U.S. dollar and 111.1 yen against the euro, which was 10.3% and 11.8% higher, respectively, than the same quarter in the previous fiscal year.&#160;&#160;On a local currency basis, consolidated sales decreased 1%.&#160;&#160;For references to sales on a local currency basis, see Note on page 10.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the CPD segment, sales decreased due to lower sales of products such as components and compact digital cameras.&#160;&#160;This decrease was partially offset by higher sales of interchangeable single lens cameras.&#160;&#160;In the NPS segment, sales decreased due to lower sales of products such as PCs.&#160;&#160;In the Pictures segment, sales decreased primarily due to lower home entertainment revenues from the current year&#8217;s film slate, as the same quarter in the previous fiscal year benefitted from the strong worldwide home entertainment performances of<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline"> Michael Jackson&#8217;s This Is It</font> and <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">2012, </font>as well as the appreciation of the yen against the U.S. dollar.&#160;&#160;In the Music segment, sales decreased primarily due to the continued decline of the physical music market and the negative impact of the appreciation of the yen against the U.S. dollar.&#160;&#160;In the Financial Services segment, revenue decreased primarily due to a decline in revenue at Sony Life and a decrease in revenue at SFI resulting mainly from the deconsolidation of its lease and rental business.&#160;&#160;The decline in revenue at Sony Life was primarily due to a decrease in net gains on sales of securities in the general account, partially offset by an increase in revenue from insurance premiums.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">An <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">operating loss </font>of 73.4 billion yen (884 million U.S. dollars) was reported, a deterioration of 17.3 billion yen compared to the loss recorded in the same quarter of the previous fiscal year.&#160;&#160;The primary factors causing the lower results include a significant decrease in operating income in the Financial Services segment described below.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the CPD segment, operating loss improved.&#160;&#160;In the same quarter of the previous fiscal year, a 27.1 billion yen non-cash charge was recorded related to LCD television asset impairment.&#160;&#160;(For reference to LCD television asset impairment, see note*** on page 2.)&#160;&#160;In addition, in the current quarter, semiconductors, reflecting strong performance of products such as image sensors, favorably impacted the changes in segment operating results.&#160;&#160;In the NPS segment, operating loss deteriorated mainly due to lower sales of PlayStation<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#174;</font>2 (&#8220;PS2&#8221;) hardware and software in the game business.&#160;&#160;In the Pictures segment, despite lower sales, operating income increased primarily due to the higher gains recognized from the purchase and sale of interests in television businesses than the gains recognized in the same quarter in the previous fiscal year, as well as lower restructuring costs.&#160;&#160;In the Music segment, operating results improved, despite lower sales, primarily due to lower restructuring, marketing and overhead costs. <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>In the Financial Services segment, operating income significantly decreased due to the increase in provisions of policy reserves for variable insurances in the separate account and the above-noted factors contributing to lower revenues in the general account at Sony Life.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Equity in net loss of affiliated companies, </font>recorded within operating income, was 0.3 billion yen (3 million U.S. dollars) compared to equity in net income of 3.1 billion yen in the same quarter of the previous fiscal year.&#160;&#160;Equity in net income of Sony Ericsson decreased by 0.5 billion yen, to 0.5 billion yen (6 million U.S. dollars) during the current quarter.&#160;&#160;This decrease was primarily due to a decline in the number of feature phones shipped.&#160;&#160;Equity in net loss for S-LCD was 1.7 billion yen (20 million U.S. dollars), compared to equity in net income of 1.4 billion yen in the same quarter of the previous fiscal year.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the current quarter, Sony recorded charges of 11.9 billion yen (143 million U.S. dollars), consisting principally of idle facility costs at manufacturing sites and an incremental provision for life insurance policy reserves, caused by the Earthquake.&#160;&#160;In addition, there was a 5.1 billion yen (61 million U.S. dollars) impact from the estimated net margin loss associated with a decrease in sales resulting from the Earthquake and an estimate of variable costs.&#160;&#160;For detail of the charges related to the Earthquake, see Consolidated Results for the Fiscal Year Ended March 31, 2011 on page 3.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The net effect of<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"> other income and expenses</font> deteriorated 3.8 billion yen (46 million U.S. dollars) primarily due to the recording of a net foreign exchange loss in the current quarter versus a net foreign exchange gain in the previous year&#8217;s fourth quarter.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Loss before income taxes</font> was 68.1 billion yen (821 million U.S. dollars), a deterioration of 21.2 billion yen, compared to the same quarter of the previous fiscal year due to the lower operating results discussed above.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Income taxes</font>: During the current quarter, Sony recorded 313.3 billion yen (3,775 million U.S. dollars) of income taxes, resulting primarily from the recording of a non-cash charge to establish a valuation allowance of 362.3 billion yen (4,365 million U.S. dollars) against certain deferred tax assets in Japan.&#160;&#160;For further details on this charge, see Consolidated Results for the Fiscal Year Ended March 31, 2011 on page 3.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Net loss attributable to Sony Corporation&#8217;s stockholders </font>for the current quarter was 388.8 billion yen (4,684 million U.S. dollars), a deterioration of 332.2 billion yen.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sales on a local currency basis described herein reflect sales obtained by applying the yen&#8217;s monthly average exchange rates in the previous fiscal year and the same quarter of the previous fiscal year to local currency-denominated monthly sales in the current fiscal year and the current quarter.&#160;&#160;Sales on a local currency basis are not reflected in Sony&#8217;s consolidated financial statements and are not measures in accordance with U.S. GAAP.&#160;&#160;Sony does not believe that these measures are a substitute for U.S. GAAP measures.&#160;&#160;However, Sony believes that disclosing sales information on a local currency basis provides additional useful analytical information to investors regarding the operating performance of Sony.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Assumed foreign currency exchange rates: approximately 83 yen to the U.S. dollar and approximately 115 yen to the euro.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Restructuring charges are expected to be approximately 25 billion yen for the Sony group in the fiscal year ending March 31, 2012 compared to 67.1 billion yen recorded in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;This amount will be recorded as an operating expense included in the above-mentioned forecast for operating income.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Equity in net income of affiliated companies for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2012 is expected to be approximately 15 billion yen, compared to equity in net income of 14.1 billion yen in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The forecast for each business segment is as follows:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">CPD</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sales are expected to increase year-on-year, despite the negative impact of the Earthquake, primarily due to higher sales in LCD televisions resulting from an anticipated increase in unit sales, and higher sales in semiconductors, which is anticipated to benefit from increased image sensor production capacity.&#160;&#160;Operating income is expected to significantly increase, primarily due to continuous cost reductions and the above-mentioned sales increase in LCD televisions, as well as a decrease in restructuring charges.&#160;&#160;The expected operating income increase is partially offset by the negative impact of the Earthquake, which is anticipated to primarily affect&#160;components and compact digital cameras.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">NPS</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sales are expected to increase year-on-year primarily due to higher sales in the game business, PCs and network services.&#160;&#160;In contrast, operating income is expected to significantly decrease, primarily due to lower unit sales of PSP<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#174;</font> (PlayStation Portable) and PS2 hardware and software, as well as expenses associated with the unauthorized access to Sony&#8217;s PlayStation<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#174;</font>Network, Qriocity<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#8482;</font> and Sony Online Entertainment network services.&#160;&#160;Please refer to the&#160;relevant section of the&#160;Management Policy on page 14 for more details.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Pictures</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sales are expected to increase year-on-year due to increases in worldwide theatrical and home entertainment revenues, television advertising and subscription revenues from SPE&#8217;s international channels, and revenues from television programming.&#160;&#160;Segment operating income is expected to decrease, primarily due to the absence of a gain from the remeasurement of a previously owned equity interest that occurred in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Music</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sales are expected to decrease and operating income is expected to decrease primarily due to the ongoing contraction of the physical music market.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sales are expected to increase due to the continued steady expansion of the business.&#160;&#160;Segment operating income is expected to decrease year-on-year mainly due to contribution of the gain on sale of securities investments resulting from portfolio changes in the securities held at Sony Life that was recorded in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;A gain on sale of securities investments resulting from portfolio changes in the securities held at Sony Life is not expected in the fiscal year ending March 31, 2012.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As is Sony&#8217;s policy, the effects of gains and losses on investments held by Sony Life, due to market fluctuations for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2012, have not been incorporated within the above forecast as Sony cannot predict where the financial markets will be after April 1, 2011.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, these market fluctuations could further impact the current forecast.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Supplemental Information</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition to operating income, Sony&#8217;s management also evaluates Sony&#8217;s performance using non-U.S. GAAP adjusted operating income.&#160;&#160;Operating income, as adjusted, which excludes equity in net income of affiliated companies and restructuring charges, is not a presentation in accordance with U.S. GAAP, and is presented to enhance investors&#8217; understanding of Sony&#8217;s operating income by providing an alternative measure that may be useful to understand Sony&#8217;s historical and prospective operating performance.</font></div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Management Policy</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(1)</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Basic Policy on Corporate Management</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sony is engaged in a wide range of businesses, including the electronics, games, movies, music, network services and financial services businesses, and the mobile phone business via a joint venture.&#160;&#160;Sony aims to improve profitability and achieve growth by (i) continuing its on-going restructuring and transformation initiatives, and (ii) using its unique strength from its broad scope of businesses to integrate its quality hardware, software, entertainment and network services assets into attractive products to be rolled out globally.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sony also strives for a sustainable increase in corporate value to earn the satisfaction of its shareholders and investors, customers, employees and other stakeholders.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(2)</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Corporate Management Strategy: Issues Facing Sony and Management&#8217;s Response to those Issues</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The world economy in general appears to be continuing the gradual pace of recovery.&#160;&#160;While growth will likely remain low for developed countries due to fiscal restructuring, high unemployment rates and stagnant housing markets, the growth rate forecasts for emerging countries, with their growing demand,<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>are higher than those forecasts for developed countries.&#160;&#160;A scenario in which emerging countries will lead world economic growth is becoming increasingly evident.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Faced with such circumstances, Sony has actively worked to achieve a strategic integration of hardware, content and networks over the past few years while establishing lateral platforms spanning production, procurement, logistics, customer service, global sales and marketing, R&amp;D and common software design, achieving steady improvements in competitiveness and profitability.&#160;&#160;In addition, Sony has worked aggressively to increase its sales of products from high-end to entry class models in emerging markets where demand is increasing due to economic growth. <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>These improvements enabled Sony to achieve a significant increase in consolidated operating income, reaching 199.8 billion yen for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2011, nearly 6.3 times that of the previous fiscal year&#8217;s amount, despite the substantial negative impact of foreign exchange rates.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sony also reorganized its core businesses of electronics and network services into two new groups as of April 1, 2011:&#160;&#160;the Consumer Products &amp; Services (&#8220;CPS&#8221;) Group, which includes all of Sony&#8217;s consumer electronics products and the network services that link them; and the Professional, Device &amp; Solutions (&#8220;PDS&#8221;) Group, which includes B2B businesses such as semiconductors and broadcasting and professional equipment, as well as the core device business, and new business fields.&#160;&#160;For details of this reorganization, please refer to the press release announced on March 10, 2011 available at the following website: <font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">http://www.sony.net/SonyInfo/News/Press/201103/11-032E/index.html</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the CPS Group, Sony is aiming to step up the pace of next-generation, groundbreaking product development in both the home and mobile segments through the swift and flexible allocation of resources to the most important business areas of consumer electronics, games, and network services.&#160;&#160;In the PDS Group, Sony plans to contribute to vertically integrated product development based on cutting-edge Sony technologies as well as core devices and to provide customers with solutions incorporating these, while also breaking into new businesses in growth areas such as the energy business field.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Through these structural reforms, Sony plans to accelerate its evolution and growth by making maximum use of its technological strengths as a corporation that provides appealing entertainment experiences and innovative solutions to customers worldwide.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In November 2009, Sony announced its aim to achieve a medium-term target of a consolidated operating margin of 5% and an ROE of 10% by the fiscal year ending March 31, 2013.&#160;&#160;Since then, Sony&#8217;s business situation has become increasingly uncertain, reflecting volatile foreign exchange rates and intensified price competition in the consumer electronics markets.&#160;&#160;Going forward, the situation is anticipated to become more challenging due to the impact of the Earthquake that occurred in March 2011.&#160;&#160;Sony plans to respond to these challenging conditions, however, by pursuing the growth strategy mentioned above under the new management structure and based on the business structural reforms accomplished up to this point.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Production at ten manufacturing sites was suspended due to damage caused by the Earthquake, though nine of them had resumed or partially resumed production by April 28, 2011.&#160;&#160;The remaining site in Tagajyo City, Miyagi Prefecture has finalized plans for resuming production.&#160;&#160;Certain domestic and overseas manufacturing sites not directly affected by the disaster have also temporarily reduced operating rates on some production lines to accommodate difficulties with the procurement of raw materials, parts and other supplies.&#160;&#160;Sony plans to continue to work for the rapid restoration of production of products for which production was affected, by reallocating inventory of raw materials and parts within the Sony group, using alternative materials or parts, and expanding sourcing for these, among other measures.</font></div>
</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sony&#8217;s network services of PlayStation<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#174;</font>Network, Qriocity<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#8482;</font> and Sony Online Entertainment came under cyber-attack in April 2011.&#160;&#160;Sony shut down the services once a possibility of unauthorized access and undefined data loss had been confirmed, and conducted an in-depth and broad-ranging investigation together with several expert firms specializing in information security to try to determine the scope of the intrusion and theft, and then made public its understanding of the scope of the data breach.&#160;&#160;Sony implemented new and additional security control measures, the mainstays of which were improving the surveillance function for monitoring new attacks, enhancing the detection function for unauthorized access and suspicious activities and increasing levels of encryption and data protection, before restoring any services.&#160;&#160;Sony began the phased restoration of the services from May 15, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The network strategy is one of Sony&#8217;s most important strategies, and Sony will continue to contribute to the protection of personal information and the development of a secure and sound networked society, while further strengthening the information control structure for the entire Sony group.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sony management views the CPD segment and the NPS segment as single operating segments.&#160;&#160;However, Sony believes that the breakdown of CPD segment and NPS segment sales and operating revenue to customers in this table is useful to investors in understanding sales by the product category in these business segments.&#160;&#160;Additionally, Sony has partially realigned its product category configuration from the first quarter of the fiscal year ended March 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;In connection with the realignment, all prior period sales amounts by product category in the table above have been restated to conform to the current presentation.&#160;&#160;In the CPD segment, Televisions includes LCD televisions; Digital Imaging includes compact digital cameras, interchangeable single lens cameras and video cameras; Audio and Video includes home audio, Blu-ray disc players and recorders; Semiconductors includes image sensors and small- and medium-sized LCD panels; Components includes batteries, recording media and data recording systems, and Professional Solutions includes broadcast- and professional-use products.&#160;&#160;In the NPS segment, Game includes game consoles and software; PC and Other Networked Businesses includes personal computers and memory-based portable audio devices.</font></div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; WIDTH: 27pt">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">4.&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Recently adopted accounting pronouncements:</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Multiple element arrangements and software deliverables -</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In October 2009, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued new accounting guidance for arrangements with multiple deliverables.&#160;&#160;Specifically, the new standard requires an entity to allocate consideration at the inception of an arrangement to all of its deliverables based on their relative selling prices.&#160;&#160;In the absence of vendor-specific objective evidence or third-party evidence of the selling prices, consideration must be allocated to the deliverables based on management&#8217;s best estimate of the selling prices.&#160;&#160;In addition, the guidance eliminates the use of the residual method of allocation.&#160;&#160;Also in October 2009, the FASB issued accounting guidance which changes revenue recognition for tangible products containing software and hardware elements.&#160;&#160;Specifically, tangible products containing software and hardware that function together to deliver the tangible products&#8217; essential functionality are scoped out of the existing software revenue recognition guidance and are accounted for under the revenue recognition guidance for multiple element arrangements.&#160;&#160;Sony adopted the new guidance on April 1, 2010.&#160;&#160;The adoption of the new guidance did not have a material impact on Sony&#8217;s results of operations and financial position.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Transfers of financial assets -</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In June 2009, the FASB issued new accounting guidance on accounting for transfers of financial assets.&#160;&#160;This guidance amends previous guidance by including: the elimination of the qualifying special-purpose entity (<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#8220;</font>QSPE<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#8221;</font>) concept; a new participating interest definition that must be met for transfers of portions of financial assets to be eligible for sale accounting; clarifications and changes to the derecognition criteria for a transfer to be accounted for as a sale; and a change to the amount of recognized gain or loss on a transfer of financial assets accounted for as a sale when beneficial interests are received by the transferor.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the guidance requires new disclosures regarding an entity&#8217;s involvement in a transfer of financial assets.&#160;&#160;Finally, existing QSPEs must be evaluated for consolidation in accordance with the applicable consolidation guidance upon the elimination of this concept.&#160;&#160;This guidance is effective for Sony as of April 1, 2010.&#160;&#160;The adoption of this guidance did not have a material impact on Sony&#8217;s results of operations and financial position.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Variable interest entities -</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In June 2009, the FASB issued new accounting guidance for determining whether to consolidate a variable interest entity (&#8220;VIE&#8221;).&#160;&#160;This guidance changes the approach for determining the primary beneficiary of a VIE from a quantitative risk and reward model to a qualitative model based on control, and requires an ongoing reassessment of whether an entity is the primary beneficiary.&#160;&#160;This guidance is effective for Sony as of April 1, 2010.&#160;&#160;The adoption of this guidance did not have a material impact on Sony&#8217;s results of operations and financial position.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; WIDTH: 27pt">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">5.&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sony realigned its reportable segments from the first quarter of the fiscal year ended March 31, 2011, to reflect modifications to the organizational structure as of April 1, 2010, primarily repositioning the operations of the previously reported B2B &amp; Disc Manufacturing segment.&#160;&#160;In connection with this realignment, the Consumer Products &amp; Devices segment was renamed the Consumer, Professional &amp; Devices (&#8220;CPD&#8221;) segment.&#160;&#160;The CPD segment includes televisions, digital imaging, audio and video, semiconductors and components as well as professional solutions (the B2B business which was previously incorporated in the B2B &amp; Disc Manufacturing segment).&#160;&#160;The equity results of S-LCD Corporation are also included within the CPD segment.&#160;&#160;The disc manufacturing business previously included in the B2B &amp; Disc Manufacturing segment is now included in All Other.&#160;&#160;The Networked Products &amp; Services, Pictures, Music and Financial Services segments remain unchanged.&#160;&#160;The equity earnings from Sony Ericsson Mobile Communications AB continue to be presented as a separate segment.&#160;&#160;In connection with the realignment, all prior period amounts in the segment disclosures have been revised to conform to the current presentation.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On April 1 2011, Sony Semiconductor Kyushu Corporation, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Sony Corporation, acquired semiconductor fabrication facilities from Toshiba Corporation (&#8220;Toshiba&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The fabrication facilities were operated by Nagasaki Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (&#8220;NSM&#8221;), a joint venture among Toshiba, Sony Corporation and Sony Computer Entertainment Inc. (&#8220;SCEI&#8221;), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Sony Corporation.&#160;&#160;The purchase price for the facilities was 53,000 million yen.&#160;&#160;NSM was dissolved on March 31, 2011, and accordingly Toshiba, Sony Corporation and SCEI terminated the NSM joint venture relationship.</font></div>
